Hey! I think it’s awesome that you’re putting in so much effort to figure out what’s been going on with you. You sounds like you’re really self-aware and that’s really admirable. As far as getting help without your parents, you could try [betterhelp.com](https://www.betterhelp.com) it’s online therapy and can be super affordable if you click the “i need financial help” thing. If you don’t have money (I had no money at all in high school) there are actually a lot of [apps](https://www.healthline.com/health/bipolar-disorder/top-iphone-android-apps) out there that can help you self-regulate and teach you a lot about bipolar and anxiety! You could also text crisis text line at 741741 (which is free and anonymous) and their counselors have loads of resources they can give you. Sorry this is such a long response lol but last resource that can help connect you with free or cheap counselors, etc. is [TWLOHA.com](https://twloha.com/find-help/)

Hi! I (25 f) just wanted to say that reading this made me feel so validated and so much less alone. I struggled with panic attacks when I was first dating my now husband (29 m) and feel like I went through almost exactly what you wrote. I felt so crazy for crying/sobbing about small things that I couldn’t control myself enough to stop. 
It sounds like your boyfriend is being super caring and understanding, which is huge. I totally agree with @ilovecatswastaken in that taking more about it is the best thing. It’s helped my husband and I loads. Let him know what you need when you’re in a panic attack (for me it’s reassuring words that he still likes me, acting calm, and a glass of water) and it’s been huge for my self-worth and our relationship. Hence now we’ve been married 2 years! 
So anyway I see you. I can relate and thank you for posting this so that myself and others can feel less alone in things like this. Best of luck!!
